Subject: Rawlin RFP: Private/on‑prem readiness questionnaire

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for taking this. Attached is our initial questionnaire for on‑prem readiness; it focuses on operator separation, patch signing, and evidence for air‑gapped maintenance windows. We need your responses to proceed with procurement and internal security review.

Key asks in the packet:
- Operator roles & separation (who has operator access in a sealed environment)
- Signed patch workflow and SBOM acceptance
- Network egress controls and evidence of validated diagrams
- Expected lead time for install and operator training

Can you confirm an expected turnaround for the filled questionnaire and what evidence you can provide (diagrams, runbooks, signed attestations)? We’re on a tight timeline and would appreciate responses by EOD Thursday (UTC).

Sara Lewis
Sr. Procurement Manager, Rawlin Systems
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rawlin RFP: Private/on‑prem readiness questionnaire

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the packet. We can complete the questionnaire and provide supporting evidence. Preliminary answers and the items we can supply quickly are below; I’ve attached the filled questionnaire (first pass) and a network diagram for the target topology.

Quick summary:
- Operator separation: Redwood supports role‑based operator accounts with distinct "install/operator/audit" roles; we can enforce one‑operator activation for maintenance windows. Formal operator rosters are supplied as part of the onboarding runbook.
- Patch signing & SBOM: We provide a signed patch workflow and an SBOM for release artifacts (VEX/SBOM snapshot). We can share a sample signed patch manifest for your review.
- Network egress: Our recommended deployment uses a locked egress gateway; we can provide the network diagram and a list of allowed endpoints for updates (can be pinned to a private mirror).
- Lead time & training: Typical on‑prem install lead time is 6–8 weeks from order acceptance (depending on procurement/hosting access). Operator training: 2 days remote + 1 day on‑site ops workshop (optional).

Attachments: rawlin_rfi_filled.xlsx (xlsx); network_diagram_v2.pdf (pdf)

I’m copying Laura (deploy ops) to confirm the training and runbook artifacts we can share. If you have particular evidence formats your security team prefers (A. signed attestations, B. scanned runbook excerpts, C. vendor code‑signing logs), let me know and we’ll prioritize.

Next steps:
1) Laura to produce operator runbook excerpt + training slate.
2) We’ll attach a sample signed patch manifest and SBOM snapshot.
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30‑min technical call with our deployment lead (Irene) to walk through the network diagram.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Attached are the runbook excerpt and the draft operator runbook PDF. I’ve kept the steps short for the security packet. Key points included:

Operator signed‑patch workflow (excerpt):
1) Customer places signed patch bundle onto approved media or private mirror (artifact includes manifest.sig and payload.tar.gz).
2) Operator verifies manifest signature against vendor public key (sha256 checksums verified).
3) Run pre‑flight checks (node health, KV cache snapshot, cpu/mem headroom).
4) Put service into maintenance mode via supervisor CLI (retains KV cache).
5) Apply patch payload and run post‑install smoke tests (test script runbook included).
6) If smoke fails, run automated rollback using retained snapshot; open ticket to vendor support and attach logs.

Included artifacts: operator_runbook_draft.pdf (pdf) — contains sample commands and rollback checklist; SBOM redaction guidance attached (Vanessa included manifest example separately).

Laura — training syllabus draft is in the drive link; Vanessa — can you attach the redacted manifest and SBOM here so I can bundle for Rawlin?

— Irene

Attachments: operator_runbook_draft.pdf (pdf)
